segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green turn arrow alone:
until permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a green turn arrow alone is the head displaying green_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn and no state other than green turn arrows (no circular indication, no straight arrow, no yellow, red or flashing arrow). Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_4a_o1).

The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate ('membership of a legal aggregate') and never replaced by the class atom ru.pedestrian.

'facing such a signal': the head of s1, at its position (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face'), lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian's position (kin.position, 'position of the body's reference point'), and the pedestrian's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') makes with the line from its position to the head an angle whose cosine is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos. Not a stand-in: dev.position is read as the place of the head only, never as a stop line or crossing ('the distance to a signal head is a different quantity'). Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2b).

'shall not enter': the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'), having overlapped none at the previous observation. 'the highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is read as its roadway: the pedestrian who faces the head from the sidewalk or the curb already lies within that width, so the only entry the words can forbid is the step onto the part the signal controls (narrowing on s4). st.roadway's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: the sidewalk') is the distinction wanted. The same reading as the index gives 'may not proceed to cross the highway' (NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1).

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian). At the judged observation it faces a traffic signal head s: s's position (dev.position) lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position (kin.position), and the cosine of the angle between the subject's heading (kin.heading) and the line from its position to s is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos; s displays a green turn arrow alone (green_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn, and no state other than green turn arrows); and at the previous observation the subject's footprint overlapped no roadway. The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_283_1d1 or NRS_484B_283_1d2 applies to the subject (a pedestrian signal permits it to proceed across), nor where NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2 or NRS_484B_283_1d4_o2 applies (a pedestrian who entered lawfully continuing to cross).
obligation: At the judged observation the subject's footprint overlaps no roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway): it does not step from the sidewalk, curb or other place off the roadway onto the roadway while it faces the green turn arrow alone.

narrowings.why: 'enter the highway' is read as coming onto the roadway. The highway's defined extent includes the sidewalk, on which a pedestrian facing the head already stands, so read literally the words would never be engaged by the pedestrians they address; the entry they forbid is the step onto the vehicular part the signal controls. Entry onto a shoulder or verge alone is not read as entry.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the sidewalk at a corner, 25 m from a vehicular head it faces (heading within 10 degrees of the line to the head) that displays green_arrow(left) alone; the pedestrian head it faces displays dont_walk_steady. At the next observation its footprint overlaps the roadway.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head the pedestrian faces displays circular_green alone; it steps onto the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no heading for the pedestrian: whether it faces the head is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the pedestrian head it faces displays walk: NRS_484B_283_1d1 applies to it and the duty of this paragraph does not.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_2b; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_2b; repeated unchanged

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green straight-through arrow alone:
may proceed straight through, but must not turn right or left.
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., green_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a green straight-through arrow alone is the head displaying green_arrow(straight) and no other state. Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a and NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), both held, claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region c (st.travel_region, the kinds 'a device can govern') whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; i of kind st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not read as a position, st.lane_enters not as presence in the intersection. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

The movement through intersection i (st.intersection) is the subject's passage from its entry (rel.occupies rising) to its exit. 'must not turn right or left': drv.motion.right_turn_through_region ('a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r') and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ('a turn to the left through region r'); a reversal, drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ('turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction through region r'), is a turn to one hand carried past a right angle and is no movement 'straight through', so it is read with them (narrowing). 'may proceed straight through': a passage for which none of the three holds; the permission adds no duty. As the index maps the arrow movements of NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, has entered intersection i from a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs): at the act's onset its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c and not i at the observation before. At some observation of the passage, from that entry to the judged observation, s displayed a green straight-through arrow alone (green_arrow(straight) and no other state). The rule is judged at the passage's recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap i, having overlapped it at the previous observation.
obligation: At that recognition none of drv.motion.left_turn_through_region, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region and drv.motion.u_turn_through_region holds for the subject and i (step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min): the passage was made straight through.

narrowings.why: 'turn right or left' is read as a passage through the intersection recognized as a right turn, a left turn or a reversal of direction (a U-turn turns to one hand beyond a right angle and is not straight through). A heading change below p.turn_heading_min, such as a lane change made inside the intersection, is read as straight through.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane c, recorded as entering intersection i and governed by head s displaying green_arrow(straight) alone; it enters i, its heading changes by +88 degrees inside i, and it leaves i while s still displays the arrow.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrow; the car passes through i with a heading change of 2 degrees and leaves it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone from before the car's entry until after its exit; the car turns left through i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no yaw rate for the car while it is inside i: which movement it made is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: s displays green_arrow(straight) alone at the car's entry into i and changes to circular_yellow alone while the car is turning left inside i; the car leaves i with a heading change of +90 degrees: the arrow was displayed for part of the passage only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: s displays green_arrow(straight) alone only while the car waits on c before its entry; from the entry to the exit s displays circular_green alone; the car turns left through i.

onset.words: the subject's entry into the intersection from its approach
onset.justification: The through-region acts begin, as their contracts state, 'at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r'.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, where the through-region acts are recognized

under_way.words: the subject inside the intersection it entered, turning or holding its heading, from its entry to its exit
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one from the entry on at which the subject still overlaps i and its heading change since the entry, integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'), is being accumulated; before the entry the integration has not begun, so the motion, not the place alone, tells the act from what preceded it.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; repeated unchanged

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green straight-through arrow alone:
may proceed straight through, but must not turn right or left.
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a green straight-through arrow alone is green_arrow(straight) and no other state. Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'Such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, as the index maps 'Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left,' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'must yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s6 reads by the closest approach. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'other vehicles': road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than the subject. Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk': the other road user's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of a travel region (st.travel_region) that enters i (st.lane_enters): the crosswalks of i's approaches. 'at the time the signal is exhibited': at the latest observation at which the head's display (dev.traffic_signal) became the green straight-through arrow alone. Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity, the factors the definition names, enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, faces traffic signal head s: it occupies a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which s governs (dev.governs), or it occupies i and has occupied it at every observation since it entered i from such a c; and s displays a green straight-through arrow alone (green_arrow(straight), no other state) at the judged observation.
obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class vehicle or of the class pedestrian, whose footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i at the judged observation, and overlapped one of them at the latest observation at which s's display became the green straight-through arrow alone: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within' is read through the other road user's presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the arrow is exhibited; whether its presence there is lawful is not judged, so the subject yields to every such road user. 'within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time' qualifies both the vehicles and the pedestrians.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Head s governing lane c, which enters i, changes to green_arrow(straight) alone while a pedestrian walks at 1.2 m/s in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the far-side approach of i; the car leaves its halt and proceeds straight at 8 m/s, the closest approach of the two centres lying 1.2 s ahead at 0.5 m, while the pedestrian is still in that crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrow; no other road user is in the scene; the car proceeds straight through i. The duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone while the car proceeds through i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not record which carriers' entrances the pedestrian's crosswalk marks: whether it is an adjacent crosswalk is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the pedestrian was on the sidewalk when s's arrow came on and stepped into the crosswalk afterwards: it was not within the crosswalk at the time the signal was exhibited, so no yield is owed to it under this paragraph and the subject complies.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady yellow signal alone:
is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a steady red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter,
when the red signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady yellow signal alone is circular_yellow and no other state (not flashing_yellow, a flashing indication, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the traffic that faced the yellow.

'enter the intersection': the subject's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') intersection i (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'), having not overlapped it at the previous observation. Not a stand-in: st.intersection is not the crosswalk or the stop line. As the index maps 'shall not enter or proceed through an intersection' (NRS_484B_270_4).

'when the red signal is exhibited': at the observation of the entry the head s that governs c (dev.governs) displays the steady red indication the yellow announced (dev.traffic_signal state circular_red), with no green arrow and no flashing yellow arrow beside it (narrowing on s6).

residues.why: The words state what the steady yellow indication tells the traffic facing it. They impose no duty and set no condition of the duty in s6, which the rule carries in full.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, occupies at the judged observation, or occupied at the previous one, a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs); and s displayed a steady yellow alone (circular_yellow, no other state) at some observation since the subject has occupied c without interruption: it faced the yellow on this approach.
obligation: The subject does not enter i while the red is exhibited: it is not the case that its footprint overlaps i at the judged observation, did not overlap i at the previous observation, and s displays circular_red at the judged observation with no green arrow and no flashing yellow arrow.

narrowings.why: 'the red signal' is read as the steady red indication the yellow precedes (circular_red). Where s displays a green arrow or a flashing yellow arrow beside the red, an entry for that arrow's movement is the arrow's signal (paragraphs 4 and 7), and this duty is not read on it.

scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane c, which enters i and is governed by head s; s displays circular_yellow alone while the car is 30 m short of i at 14 m/s; s changes to circular_red alone 3 s later, and the car's footprint comes to overlap i 0.5 s after the red appears.

scenarios.narrative: Same yellow; the car's footprint comes to overlap i while s still displays circular_yellow alone.

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a flashing yellow turn arrow, displayed alone or in combination with another signal:
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal,
or other such movement as is permitted by other signal indications displayed at the same time.
to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk
to other traffic lawfully within the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., flashing_yellow_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a flashing yellow turn arrow is flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn; 'displayed alone or in combination with another signal': whatever other states the head displays with it.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'enter the intersection': the passage through intersection i (st.intersection) from the entry (rel.occupies rising) to the exit. 'only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal': the movement made, recognized at the exit, is a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region, 'a turn to the left through region r'), a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region), a reversal (drv.motion.u_turn_through_region, 'turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction through region r'), or straight through where none of them holds; it must be the movement the flashing yellow arrow's direction (dev.traffic_signal) indicates: a left arrow the turn to the left and the U-turn, a right arrow the right turn, a u_turn arrow the U-turn. As the index maps the arrow movements of NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

'other signal indications displayed at the same time': the other states dev.traffic_signal displays ('several states may be displayed at once') at the same observation as the flashing yellow turn arrow. A movement they permit: circular_green, circular_yellow or flashing_yellow permit every movement; a green, yellow or flashing yellow arrow permits the movement of its direction (left: the left turn and the U-turn; right: the right turn; u_turn: the U-turn; straight: the straight movement).

operationalizations.standard: cautiously (the manner of the permitted entry)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: an entry is cautious where, at the observation of the entry, while the subject's speed is above the halt tolerance, no other road user's centre has a closest approach to the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance)

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, has entered intersection i from a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs): at the act's onset its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c and not i at the observation before. At some observation of the passage, from that entry to the judged observation, s displayed a flashing yellow turn arrow (flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn), alone or with other states. The rule is judged at the passage's recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap i, having overlapped it at the previous observation. The duty does not apply where, at such an observation of the passage at which s displayed the flashing yellow turn arrow, another state s displayed at the same observation permits the movement made (exception s5).
obligation: At the recognition the movement made through i — a left turn, a right turn or a U-turn where drv.motion.left_turn_through_region, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region or drv.motion.u_turn_through_region holds for the subject and i (step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min), straight through where none holds — is the movement indicated by a flashing yellow turn arrow s displayed at an observation of the passage (left: the left turn or the U-turn; right: the right turn; u_turn: the U-turn); and the entry was cautious: at the entry observation, while the subject's speed was above p.halt_speed_tolerance, no other road user's closest approach to it (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon) was at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The movement is read from the passage through the intersection, recognized at the exit: a left turn, a right turn or a reversal by the turn concepts, straight through where none holds (a heading change below p.turn_heading_min). A left arrow is read as indicating the U-turn as well as the left turn, a U-turn being a turn to the left carried on.
'cautiously' names no factor; it is read only through the absence of a traffic conflict with any road user at the observation of entry, the time the words fix it to ('cautiously enter').

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a flashing yellow turn arrow, displayed alone or in combination with another signal:
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal,
or other such movement as is permitted by other signal indications displayed at the same time.
to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk
to other traffic lawfully within the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., flashing_yellow_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a flashing yellow turn arrow is flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn, with whatever other states the head displays ('alone or in combination with another signal').

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'Such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'must yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the pedestrian from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s8 reads. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of a travel region (st.travel_region) that enters i (st.lane_enters). Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance. As the index maps 'lawfully within the adjacent crosswalk' (NRS_484B_307_4a_o2).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the pedestrian arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, faces traffic signal head s showing a flashing yellow turn arrow: either it occupies a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which s governs (dev.governs), and s displays flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn (with or without other states) at the judged observation; or it occupies i, has occupied it at every observation since it entered i from such a c, and s displayed such an arrow at that entry.
obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian and whose footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i at the judged observation: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within' is read through the pedestrian's presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk; whether its presence there is lawful is not judged, so the subject yields to every such pedestrian.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
a person driving a motorcycle, moped or trimobile or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
may proceed straight through or turn right or left
(1) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device
and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(2) No other device at the place prohibits
either or both such turns, if applicable;
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is circular_red and no other state (not flashing_red, and no arrow beside it). The head s is the one governing the rider's approach carrier (s7). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' requires the halt itself (rule 5), with every qualification of the requirement it names, borrowed from NRS-484B-307-8a (reference s3): 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A stop required is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement': drv.motion.complete_halt. The place: the stop line (st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') recorded as marking the entrance of the rider's carrier c (st.entrance_of), else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at the intersection (st.intersection); the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance), on the approach that ends in this entry, as NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states the place, zone and history bound. Not compliance with that node, which a composed rule grants where it is not engaged; st.region_geometry is not occupancy.

The admitted aggregates for the defined words: DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels'), DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine'), DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'trimobile' has no applicable definition and is not an aggregate: it is carried by ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants', the class atom that denotes a three-wheeled motor vehicle; the atom has no stand-in exclusion that applies. 'driving' and 'riding' are read through the road user's controlled motion (narrowing).

'may proceed straight through or turn right or left': the rider's entry into intersection i (st.intersection), its footprint coming to overlap i (rel.occupies) having occupied at the observation before a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); every movement through i is admitted. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'the applicable official traffic-control device': the signal installation of the intersection the rider is at, observed through its heads: the traffic signal heads (dev.traffic_signal) that govern (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection); the head s governing c is the rider's own. 'official' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'placed or erected by a public authority') is presumed from the head's presence (narrowing). 'waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows': from the latest onset of its halt at the place until its entry into i the rider does not overlap i, and in that interval some head of the installation begins a green indication (circular_green or a green_arrow, the lights or lighted arrows that come on once in each cycle of the installation) at least two times: a count of that head's rising green indications since the halt's onset, against the literal two.
'the signal does not change': the rider's head s (dev.traffic_signal) displays the steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at every observation from the latest onset of the halt to the entry.

'No other device at the place prohibits': a regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', codes no_left_turn and no_right_turn) governing (dev.governs) the rider's carrier c (st.travel_region) or the intersection i (st.intersection). Not a stand-in: 'a prohibition sign is a condition', and it is read as one, not as a manoeuvre. 'official' status is presumed from presence.

'either or both such turns, if applicable': the turn the rider makes on this passage through intersection i (st.intersection), from its entry (rel.occupies rising) to its exit, recognized at the exit as a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region, 'a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r') or a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region); 'if applicable': only a turn made brings a prohibition into play, and a straight passage is never prohibited by a turn sign. Read from each observation of the passage at the recognition the passage reaches, so that the condition is decided at the entry where the exit is recorded.

'yields': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a rider that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s14 reads. As the index maps 'must yield' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians and other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian and DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the rider. 'proceeding': moving, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'as directed by the signal at the intersection': it overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a travel region that enters i (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), or it occupies a travel region c' entering i that is governed (dev.governs) by a head displaying a green indication (dev.traffic_signal: circular_green or green_arrow). Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the rider grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

compositions.quote: must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection
compositions.why: The words borrow the requirement's place and its order (the crosswalk on the nearest side, or the place a sign or pavement marking indicates, else the intersection's edge) and the meaning of stopping before it. The condition requires that the halt itself occurred there; a composition with NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 would not establish it, since a composed rule counts as complied with where it is not engaged, and this paragraph governs riders whether or not that duty engages them (a bicycle or electric scooter is no vehicle). So the borrowed words are carried by the halt, the place and the approach on s2, and no rule of NRS-484B-307-8a need apply, hold or be complied with.

residues.why: The words give the cause of the unchanged red. A head that keeps its steady red alone through two complete cycles of the installation's other indications while the rider waits at its stop place has not served the rider's approach, which is a malfunction or a failure to detect the rider; the duty is the same whichever of the two causes holds, and neither shows in the scene beyond the unchanged red (s8) and the cycles (s7), which the rule reads.

applicability: The subject is of one of the classes motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (admitted aggregates) or a ru.motorcycle (the trimobile). It approached intersection i through a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs), and halted (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the place of the stop on that approach: the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance, else the crosswalk recorded as marking it, else c's entrance end at i, with the zone (p.stop_point_tolerance) and the history bound NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states. From the latest onset of that halt until its entry into i, s displayed a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at every observation and the subject's footprint did not overlap i; in that interval some traffic signal head governing a travel region that enters i began a green indication (circular_green or a green_arrow rising) at least two times (literal 2). The subject then entered i (its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c at the observation before) while s still displayed the steady red alone, and its footprint has overlapped i at every observation since that entry, the judged one included. It is not the case that the passage through i begun at that entry is recognized at its exit (at the judged observation or a later one: the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap i) as a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region; step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min) while a regulatory sign coded no_right_turn governs c or i, nor as a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region) while one coded no_left_turn governs c or i; where no such sign governs, this condition holds whatever the movement, and where one governs and the exit is not recorded, it is unknown.
obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian or of the class traffic and is proceeding as directed by the signal at i — its speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, and either its footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i, or it occupies a travel region c' entering i governed by a head that displays circular_green or a green_arrow: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'driving' and 'riding' are read through the road user's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at its controls.
'official' traffic-control device: the presence of the signal heads at the intersection is the evidence of their official status.

'proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection' is read through the signal state governing the other road user's approach (a green indication) where it approaches, and through its presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk where it is there; a road user that entered against its own red and is now within the intersection is yielded to as well.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, enters intersection i at the judged observation: its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) there and did not at the previous observation, at which it occupied a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs); and s displays at the judged observation a steady red alone (circular_red and no other state).
obligation: Rule 4c duty: an act at a place before an event. Event: the entry into i just described; each such entry is its own occurrence. Place: the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of) where one is; else the crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance; else c's entrance end at the edge of i. Where a mark's association with c is not observed, whether it governs is unknown; where its list of entrances is observed and excludes c, it does not govern and the next place in that order is read. segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme right of the highway
only when the intersecting highway is two-directional or one-way to the right,
or vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme left of a one-way highway
only when the intersecting highway is one-way to the left,
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' requires the halt itself (rule 5), with every qualification of the requirement it names, borrowed from NRS-484B-307-8a (reference s3): 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'.
